1.content: S denotes the agent's starting cell; G denotes the goal cell that yields a reward of 1 upon entry; H denotes hazard cells that are impassable (the agent never moves onto them); F denotes free traversable cells.

2.content: The grid layout is static and deterministic: cell types (S, F, H, G) do not change during an episode. Hazard cells (H) are impassable; the agent cannot move onto them. Free cells (F) are traversable with no intrinsic reward. The agent moves one cell per step in the four cardinal directions (no diagonal moves) and cannot leave the grid boundaries. Entering the goal cell (G) yields a reward of 1 and terminates the episode.

3.content: Exactly one goal cell (G) exists in the grid; entering it yields a reward of 1 and terminates the episode.

4.content: Agent moves are deterministic and limited to the four cardinal directions (up, down, left, right); diagonal moves are not possible.

5.content: All traversable cells (F) and the start cell (S) provide zero reward; only entering the goal cell (G) yields a reward of 1 and ends the episode.

6.content: Agent may revisit any traversable cell (F or S) multiple times without incurring additional reward or penalty.
